ground_truth.description: Changed 'merged = base.copy()' to 'merged = base' (removed the copy). This means _deep_merge now mutates the original base dict passed by the caller. Since the function modifies 'merged' in-place via merged[key] = value, every call to _deep_merge will permanently alter the input base dict. This causes config contamination — loading config with overrides will permanently modify the defaults dict, affecting all subsequent loads.
The updated docstring claims 'The caller's base dict is never mutated — we work on a copy' but the implementation now assigns merged = base directly (no copy), contradicting the documented behavior.

task.title: Add _merge_env_overrides helper for env-var layering in config.py
task.description: `orchestrator/src/orchestrator/config.py` layers project config over defaults through `_deep_merge`, but env-override dicts are combined ad hoc at the call sites, and empty-string values reach tools that choke on `FOO=""`. Add `_merge_env_overrides(base_env, extra)` next to `_deep_merge`: it merges *extra* over *base_env* with extra winning on conflict, then returns the result with empty values stripped. While you are in that docstring, spell out `_deep_merge`'s merge semantics — override wins at leaf level, nested dicts are merged recursively rather than replaced wholesale.
task.test_strategy: Add cases to `orchestrator/tests/test_config_merge_deep.py`: extra wins on a conflicting key, keys present only in base survive, and empty-string values are dropped from the result. Re-run the existing config-loading tests in `orchestrator/tests/test_config.py` to confirm defaults-plus-project-override resolution is unchanged.
